title: Stream pacer and kernel advisor for tail-latency stabilization
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Reduce 95th/99th tail latency for continuous batching workloads by coordinating admission pacing with kernel selection and attention prewarming. Introduce a Stream Pacer that smooths arrivals at the admission gate and a Kernel Advisor service that recommends per-batch kernel/execution paths at admission time.
background: We continue to see spikes in tail latency for mixed short/long sequence workloads. Current admission logic treats requests uniformly, and kernel selection occurs after batches are formed causing suboptimal kernel handoffs and late failures to satisfy SLOs. Attention prewarm is opportunistic today and not coordinated with prefill/ decode scheduling. Prior tickets improved batch shaping heuristics, but end-to-end coordination between admission, kernel choice and attention warm paths is missing.
goals: 1) Reduce 95th/99th latency by 20-30% for mixed sequence traffic; 2) Avoid kernel rebinds mid-decode that cause stalls; 3) Ensure prefill attention state is warmed for likely decode paths; 4) Add observability surfaces to validate decisions.
non_goals: 1) Replace existing kernel selection runtime; 2) Fully rewrite admission controller in this sprint; 3) Solve all workload diversity problems — focus on highest-traffic service tiers first.
proposed_design: Architecture: insert Stream Pacer component in front of admission gate to smooth instantaneous arrivals using an elastic token bucket tuned by recent queue depth and observed decode latencies. At admission time the Kernel Advisor evaluates the incoming request shape (seq_len, temperature, user tier, model variant) and recommends a kernel profile and attention prewarm plan (none / partial / full). The admission controller uses the kernel recommendation to decide batch membership and prefill routing. Prefill and decode scheduling handshake: prefill emits an attention-warm token that the decode stage can claim; if unclaimed within a short TTL, token is invalidated to avoid stale caches.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th latency reduced by >=20% on A/B for targeted traffic; 2) Kernel Advisor accuracy (prediction of needed kernel profile) >=85% vs baseline post-hoc labeling; 3) No increased CPU/GPU utilization >10% vs baseline; 4) Dashboards show decreased kernel rebind events during decode; 5) E2E tests for token TTL and fallback behavior.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype Stream Pacer + simple Kernel Advisor (rule-based) behind feature flag; add tracing hooks and counters. Phase 2: Integrate with admission controller, add attention token handshake and TTL. Phase 3: Replace rule-based advisor with lightweight ML model (if Phase 1 success). Phase 4: Rollout to canary hosts then full fleet with progressive traffic ramp.
tasks: Design Stream Pacer token-bucket parameters and control loop
Implement Kernel Advisor API and rule-set for initial rollout
Add attention-warm token lifecycle and TTL enforcement
Integrate advisor decision into admission batcher
Add tracing, metrics, and dashboards (kernel_decisions, attention_tokens, rebind_events)
Run A/B experiment and collect acceptance metrics
Iterate advisor rules or train lightweight model based on experiment data
tradeoffs: Smoothing arrivals adds controlled delay to some requests (configurable latency knob) in exchange for lower tail variance. Kernel Advisor increases control-plane logic complexity and may suggest suboptimal kernels early; mitigations: conservative defaults and quick fallback. Attention prewarm tokens consume limited cache budget; risk of cache pollution addressed via TTL and eviction heuristics.
risks: 1) Misconfigured pacer may increase P50 for small fraction of traffic; 2) Advisor mispredictions cause unnecessary kernel switches; 3) Cache mis-warms reduce overall throughput; 4) Observability gaps hide regressions during rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged rollout on staging with synthetic mixed workloads; 2) Canary on 5% of production hosts (non-critical tenants) for 48h; 3) Evaluate metrics and rollback if >=10% regression in P99 or CPU/GPU >10% above baseline; 4) Expand to 25% then 100% with gradual parameter tuning.
observability: Add structured spans: StreamPacer.enqueue, KernelAdvisor.recommend, Admission.assign_batch, AttentionWarm.emit, Decode.claim_warm_token. Expose per-tenant counters and histogram of advisor confidence. Add dashboard comparing canary vs baseline and enable alerts on P99 regressions and rebind surge.
testing: Unit tests for pacer control loop and token lifecycle. Integration tests simulating mixed short+long sequences and verifying attention token handoff. Load test in perf lab to quantify GPU utilization and tail reduction. Chaos tests: drop attention tokens, force advisor miss and verify graceful fallback.
migration_notes: Introduce default-safe parameters to avoid visible user impact if feature enabled by accident. Kernel Advisor config should be stored in config service with versioned rollout. Provide kill-switch and quick disable via feature-flagging.
documentation: Confluence doc: Stream Pacer design + Kernel Advisor decision matrix; README for runtime operators with tuning knobs and recommended defaults. Update runbook for tail-latency incidents to include advisor kill-switch steps.
